chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Illinois Jacquet and Lionel Hampton's first band
summary: After a break, Jackson first heard Jacquet in Hampton's 1941 band and lists its saxophones, trumpets, and rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Let's take a little breather for a second so you can finish your repast there and then we'll go back into something else, get into some other --
Now, where are you on the notes, so we --
Yeah, yeah, here we are, Butter.
We've just taken our little break now.

I'd just like to mention we were talking about the great saxophone players, Don, Ed Inge and Don Byers and we named -- we didn't even mention Jacquet Jackett. Of course, that's coming up later, but when did you first run into Jacquet Jackett? In Cab's band? He came --
Oh, no, uh-uh.
No?
Uh-uh.
Illinois Jacquet Jackett, that is.
I first heard Jacquet Jackett with the first band that Lionel Hampton had in 1941. That's when I first heard him.
Well, he came in here with Lionel around that time.
Yes. And Lionel had a very good band there.
That's right.
And it was -- the two tenor players was like Mutt and Jeff, here was Dexter Gordon, and Dexter Gordon was so tall and Illinois was short, and they was the two tenor players in there.
Right.
And the alto players in the band was Marshall Royal and Ray Perry, and the baritone player was the co-writer of 'Open the Door, Richard.' I'll think of his name a little later.
But the trumpets in that band was Ernie Royal, Joe Newman, and Karl George.
Right.

And the trombone player, we called him Mushmouth. I forget his real name. And the trombone player was a beautiful trombone player. And, of course, Norman was the bass player. I think he's out in Frisco now.
No, not Norman. He was a football player. He lives in San Francisco. He --
Freckle face guy.
Yes, yes.
He was the bass player, anyway.
I can't recall his name.
And, of course, Milt Buckner was the pianist.
Right.
And the guitar player used to be with Nat Cole. He was the guitar player then.
Irvin Ashby.
Yeah, he was the guitar player.
Irvin Ashby.
Irvin Ashby. He was the guitar player with Hamp then.
I'm ashamed I can't recall the bass player's name, as well as I know him.
Uh-huh, that was --
He turned out to be a disc jockey later in San Francisco.
Uh-huh.

The last time I saw him, you know, he was playing with a relief band. We played a dance there -- a concert, rather -- and he was playing in the concert band, you know, and he played a little while in a club there, but --
